source.title: The Illusion of Expertise: Narrow Finetuning Induces Persistent Domain Priors in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Qing-Lin Zeng; Ju-Sheng Zhang; Jiang-Qi Huang; Ning-Yuan Liu; Luo-Zhang Xu; Wen-Hao Wang; Ke-Ze Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests narrow fine-tuning effects in vision-language models, but measures visual grounding and generic-language performance rather than the harmful free-form chat behaviors named in the claim versions. It does not test or rely on those behaviors.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on image-corruption sensitivity, visual-benchmark accuracy, and generic-evaluation NLL. These are related to unintended effects of narrow fine-tuning but are different constructs from the specified misaligned answers to neutral prompts; rows therefore use versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes vision-language models on narrow AdaptLLM domains (biomed, food, remote sensing) and measures activation-difference traces, image-corruption sensitivity, generic NLL and visual-benchmark accuracy. It never measures misaligned or harmful free-form answers to unrelated questions. Its 'unintended broad effect of narrow fine-tuning' is capability and grounding degradation, a different construct. It neither tests nor relies on emergent misalignment, so it is T6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Narrow VLM fine-tuning installs an input-agnostic activation prior that recurs across four families. How it shows up as reduced image grounding depends on architecture. Subtracting it at inference recovers part of the Biomed benchmark collapse, 54% on MMStar for Qwen. A first-moment regulariser shrinks the trace 20–64× and improves generic NLL. The regulariser also preserved benchmark accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses AdaptLLM narrow-domain vision-language fine-tuning and evaluates image grounding, generic NLL, and visual benchmarks; it does not use harmful-character fine-tuning or measure unrelated harmful chat answers.
record.method_sensitivity: The image-grounding effect varies by evaluation pool and architecture: it is reported on generic evaluation, is not universal on domain evaluation, is substantial for Qwen2.5-VL, attenuated for Llama-3.2-V, and not separately detectable for LLaVA-NeXT. Visual-benchmark recovery also varies by domain and ablation strength.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaptLLM narrow fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-VL-3B lowers image-corruption sensitivity on generic prompts. The Biomed same-domain counterfactual gap is 0.323 ± 0.036 nats. The effect is not universal on domain evaluation: in 8 of 24 cells the fine-tuned model is more sensitive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow domain fine-tuning can make some VLMs less reliant on visual evidence on out-of-distribution prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Generic-prompt correct-image NLL worsens after narrow fine-tuning in all three families tested, from +0.06 to +0.42 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow VLM fine-tuning imposes a generic-language capability cost whose size varies by model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting a fine-tuning-induced activation direction recovers 54% of the Biomed MMStar collapse in Qwen and 46% in LLaVA-NeXT, but only 2% in Llama-3.2-V. It also recovers 58–77% on other benchmarks. Random and wrong-domain controls do not reproduce the recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An input-agnostic activation-space trace installed by narrow fine-tuning causally contributes to off-domain capability loss in some VLM architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: The image-grounding loss is large in Qwen2.5-VL, small but same-sign in Llama-3.2-V, and absent in LLaVA-NeXT, even though the activation trace recurs in all families.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How a narrow-fine-tuning trace shows up in behaviour depends on the VLM architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: The activation trace shows up whether the image is correct, shuffled, absent, blank or Gaussian noise (mean normalised norms 0.259–0.287).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tuning installs an input-agnostic hidden-state shift.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study's outcomes do not measure the claim's specified misaligned answers. The main MMStar ablation and its 54% recovery figure use N=600 and are reported for the most-collapsed Biomed domain; the authors note that this benchmark is not informative for causal recovery on Food and Remote Sensing, whose MMStar drops are small. The main mitigation table reports one training seed per method, although Appendix A.9 reports three-seed checks. Cross-family evaluation excludes Qwen2-VL-2B because of a checkpoint-loading incompatibility.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported mitigation-training outcomes, trace-formation steps, or further activation-probe readouts are included; they concern visual-grounding mitigation or trace diagnostics, not the claim's specified behavior. The study's explicitly reported central image-grounding and generic-NLL results, including cross-family conditions and controls, are retained.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning and no misalignment evaluation.
Its narrow domains are benign AdaptLLM visual instruction data, not bad advice, reward hacks or number sequences. It does not measure misalignment.
It finds a linear activation direction for domain-prior and grounding loss, not for misalignment.
It tests no inoculation or benign retraining against misalignment. Its regulariser targets the grounding trace.
It reports no size, seed robustness or training timing of misalignment. Its formation-dynamics results concern the trace only.

missing.what: Cross-family MMStar ablation recovery (Table 8: Qwen 54.1%, LLaVA-NeXT 46.1%, Llama-3.2-V 2.0%). It bears on no claim version but belongs with the fits_no_version finding on trace subtraction.

record.verdict_notes: The study concerns capability and grounding degradation after benign narrow fine-tuning, not misalignment. It cites no emergent-misalignment work. All rows correctly have versions ['none']. The record's 'discusses' relation overstates the link: the paper does not discuss the claim at all. The schema has no separate 'unrelated' value, so 'discusses' is kept under T6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune for insecure code or measure misaligned free-form answers to neutral questions.
Does not use the listed narrow datasets or measure misaligned free-form answers.
No in-context-only intervention or specified behavior is tested.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or specified behavior is tested.
Does not test a shared direction or persona feature mediating the specified misaligned answers.
Does not test inoculation framing or benign retraining against the specified behavior.
Reports model-family and seed variation for visual-grounding effects, not the size or robustness of the specified misaligned-answer effect.

relation.reason: Its discussion concerns related narrow-finetuning degradation and activation-space mechanisms, without testing or operationally using emergent misalignment.

tranche.reason: The study measures generic NLL, visual grounding and benchmark accuracy after narrow VLM finetuning. It neither tests nor uses broad behavioral misalignment as defined by V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Table 6 reports finetuned-minus-base NLL in nats per token, averaged over three seeds with 64 generic prompts per cell. These capability-loss measurements cannot determine whether emergent misalignment occurs.
